title: activestorage blob isn't created with ArgumentError when initialized by nested attributes
body:
### Steps to reproduce
<!-- (Guidelines for creating a bug report are [available
here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#creating-a-bug-report)) -->

First, create has_many association between `:shops` and `:members` with nested attributes and activestorage declaration.

```ruby
class CreateShops < ActiveRecord::Migration[6.0]
  def change
    create_table :shops do |t|
      t.string :name
    end
    create_table :members do |t|
      t.bigint :shop_id
      t.string :name
    end
  end
end
class Shop < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :members
  accepts_nested_attributes_for :members
end
class Member < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :shop
  has_one_attached :image
end
```

Then, creating blob with nested attributes always fails with ArgumentError, while direct creation gets success.

```ruby
Shop.create!(name: :hello)

Member.create!(name: :test, shop_id: Shop.first.id, image: {io: StringIO.new('test'), filename: :test})
# => success

Shop.create!(
  name: :shop,
  members_attributes: [
    {name: :test1, image: {io: StringIO.new('test1'), filename: :test1}},
    {name: :test2, image: {io: StringIO.new('test2'), filename: :test2}}
  ]
)
# => ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments (given 1, expected 0; required keywords: io, filename))
```

I guess the cause is with nested attributes it converts arguments to indifferent access hash.

https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/66cabeda2c46c582d19738e1318be8d59584cc5b/activerecord/lib/active_record/nested_attributes.rb#L500

While, building methods of ActiveStorage::Blob expect keyword arguments.

https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/66cabeda2c46c582d19738e1318be8d59584cc5b/activestorage/app/models/active_storage/blob.rb#L60

### Expected behavior
<!-- Tell us what should happen -->

Create, associate, upload blob successfully using nested attributes.

### Actual behavior
<!-- Tell us what happens instead -->

Fail with the following error.
`ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments (given 1, expected 0; required keywords: io, filename))`

### System configuration
**Rails version**:
6.0.0
**Ruby version**:
2.5.1p57

I'm not sure the best way to fix this issue, but please check this behavior once.
